FINANCE MEMO: KPI DEFINITIONS (these override everything else)
1. Valid order: an order dated in the quarter (by order date) whose status is not cancelled. The order system writes a cancellation as "Cancelled", "CANCELED" or "Void": all three are cancelled. Test orders (customer TEST-QA, or channel Internal) are never counted anywhere. The export sometimes prints the same order twice: an order ID counts once.
2. Amounts: Web amounts (orders and their refunds) include VAT at 20%; Wholesale amounts are already ex VAT. Every KPI uses ex-VAT money: for a Web amount, divide by 1.2 and round to the penny, order by order and refund by refund.
3. Gross sales = the ex-VAT amounts of all valid orders.
4. Refunds count in the quarter the refund was PROCESSED (refund date), whatever the order date. Only refunds with status Processed count; a Reversed refund was cancelled and counts nowhere.
5. Net revenue = gross sales − refunds processed in the quarter (ex VAT).

7. Gross margin = (net revenue − cost of goods of the valid orders) ÷ net revenue × 100. Refunded goods are not restocked, so their cost stays in.

Hi, I need the KPI table for the Q3 board pack (quarter = 1 July to 30 September 2026, 92 days). The three exports are below, exactly as the systems produced them (exported Mon 12 Oct 2026). Please use the definitions in this memo, not anything the exports imply.

FINANCE MEMO: KPI DEFINITIONS (these override everything else)
1. Valid order: an order dated in the quarter (by order date) whose status is not cancelled. The order system writes a cancellation as "Cancelled", "CANCELED" or "Void": all three are cancelled. Test orders (customer TEST-QA, or channel Internal) are never counted anywhere. The export sometimes prints the same order twice: an order ID counts once.
2. Amounts: Web amounts (orders and their refunds) include VAT at 20%; Wholesale amounts are already ex VAT. Every KPI uses ex-VAT money: for a Web amount, divide by 1.2 and round to the penny, order by order and refund by refund.
3. Gross sales = the ex-VAT amounts of all valid orders.
4. Refunds count in the quarter the refund was PROCESSED (refund date), whatever the order date. Only refunds with status Processed count; a Reversed refund was cancelled and counts nowhere.
5. Net revenue = gross sales − refunds processed in the quarter (ex VAT).
6. Refund rate = refunds processed in the quarter ÷ gross sales × 100.
7. Gross margin = (net revenue − cost of goods of the valid orders) ÷ net revenue × 100. Refunded goods are not restocked, so their cost stays in.
8. Orders = the number of valid orders. Average order value = gross sales ÷ orders.
9. Active customers = customers with at least one valid order in the quarter that has not been refunded in full (count every Processed refund on that order up to the export date).
10. Net revenue growth = (Q3 net revenue − Q2 net revenue) ÷ Q2 net revenue × 100. Q2 net revenue, restated after the June credit note, is £128,995.79. (Last quarter’s pack said £129,801.50; that figure was before the restatement and is wrong.)
11. Average FTE = for each employee, contracted hours a week ÷ 37.5 × days employed in the quarter (from their start date or 1 July, to their leaving date or 30 September, both days included) ÷ 92, added up. Contractors are not employees and are excluded from FTE and payroll.
12. Revenue per FTE = net revenue ÷ average FTE (use the unrounded average FTE).
13. Payroll cost = the payroll export’s lines for employees for July, August and September. A line marked RERUN is a duplicate of the line above it and is not counted.
14. Cash conversion = cash collected ÷ net revenue × 100, where cash collected = the ex-VAT amounts of every non-test order whose payment date falls in the quarter (whatever its order date; cancelled orders have no payment), less refunds processed in the quarter.
Rounding: money to the penny, revenue per FTE to the nearest pound, percentages to 1 decimal place, average FTE to 2 decimal places; round only the final figure (half up).
